God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power, love and self-control. Where do you need that today?
Timothy's faith first lived in his grandmother and mother. Who passed faith on to you?
Paul says, "I know whom I have believed." What do you know about the one you have believed?
Onesiphorus often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chains. Who could you refresh?
Paul uses the soldier, athlete and farmer as examples. Which picture helps you most?
"If we are faithless, he remains faithful." What comfort does this give you?
"Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved." How do you handle God's word?
The Lord's servant must be kind and patient with those who oppose. How can you respond kindly to opposition?
Paul describes people who love pleasure more than God. Where might your loves be out of order?
Paul reminds Timothy of his own faith, patience and love in persecution. Whose example has helped you?
Timothy had known the Scriptures from childhood. How can you pass on Scripture to the next generation?
All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable. How has Scripture equipped you?
Paul says to be ready in season and out of season. What does faithfulness look like when it's hard?
Paul says, "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith." What do you want said of your life?
Paul was deserted, but the Lord stood by him. When has the Lord stood by you when others didn't?
Paul ends with greetings to friends and co-workers. Who are the friends who keep you going?
